newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen mixed, impetus missing.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen mixed, impetus missing.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen mixed on Thursday with upward impetus missing during the corporate reporting season, dealers said.
"The drifting isn't being caused by anything significant, it's just part of the up and down of the results season," said one local dealer.
"There's nothing happening at all on the institutional side at this time of year," another dealer said.
Singapore shares ended Wednesday weaker, with the key Straits Times Industrials Index falling 17.36 points to 2,177.39.
Two results eagerly anticipated by dealers on Wednesday, Cycle & Carriage and Malayan Credit, were unlikely to have bolstered confidence, dealers said.
"We were expecting a 20-odd percent rise in earnings," said one dealer disappointed with the 14 percent lift reported last night for Malayan Credit's 1996 year.
Motor retailer Cycle & Carriage reported a 10 percent rise in 1996 profits but described its 1997 outlook as "challenging" as competition would remain stiff.
